item.title: Calls for cooperation as ASEAN summit awaits Trump
item.description:
President Trump's trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin has the makings of an unpredictable spectacle — and that's exactly what has U.S. allies anxious. Why it matters: Trump's stated goal for the first-ever summit between the nations' three leaders is to start a discussion on nuclear disarmament. But the fear is that he could go off script and take positions on Ukraine or Taiwan that undermine their interests or appear to side with their chief adversaries, according to several European officials and Western diplomats. "We know that every time President Trump talks to or sees Putin, it translates into bad news for Ukraine and for Europe. We brace for anything," a European diplomat told Axios. item.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
item.description:
Bullet hit 72-year-old Fadha Wadha in head outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, in the West Bank, say residents A 72-year-old Palestinian woman has been shot dead in an overnight attack by Israeli settlers in a village near Jericho where settlers have recently moved in after taking over several Palestinian homes. Fadha Wadha was standing outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta in the occupied West Bank when she was struck in the head by a bullet as Israeli settlers fired towards Palestinian houses, according to testimonies from residents. item.title: More than 100,000 take part in France pay protests
item.description:
French protests driven by frustration over the cost of living and public services resume today, with economists offering a bleak prognosis for one of Europe’s biggest economies. The French government is grappling with sky-high debt, a worrying deficit, and slow growth , while public anger has propelled a far-right party into the driver’s seat for 2027 presidential elections. That latter scenario is now “the key source of uncertainty,” Goldman Sachs said in a note to clients. Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, warned that while France in theory had numerous paths — to fiscal consolidation as well as fiscal crisis — “they are not equal in number and width … There is an Autobahn to wider spreads and a narrow back alley to much tighter ones.” — Prashant Rao

item.title: NASA's Voyager 1 reaches a light-day away from Earth
item.description:
Humans have trouble with inhuman distances. Miles are about the largest comprehensible unit of measurement we have, because we can understand miles. Watering hole is in a mile? No problem, we’ll be there soon. Aurochs herd is 30 miles away? OK, our hunting party won't walk that in a day, but it’s doable. Miles are a good measure for us, and on the scale of the universe, absolutely useless. The Sun is about 93 million miles from Earth. Can that possibly be spatially encompassed by a human mind that evolved to think in terms of footsteps? The nearest star after that is about 25 trillion miles away. We have the words, but they blur into a meaningless litany of zeroes and -illions. How big is the observable universe? 546,710,000,000,000,000,000,000 miles across, best we can tell. item.title: New York Is Fed Up With Chuck Schumer
item.description:
When did New York voters begin to turn on their five-term U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer? Was it when he squandered Democratic leverage to hash out a deal to avoid a government shutdown last year? (Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez called that move a "betrayal.") Or perhaps it was his April vote, along with just six other Democrats , to continue sending military bulldozers to Israel, at a moment when Americans are increasingly fed up with Israel's war in Gaza. Maybe they thought Schumer had lost touch with reality when he refused to endorse Zohran Mamdani last year, a decision that was echoed in his failure to recognize other progressive juggernauts across the country before the 2026 midterms.
